The tender agent was woken 6 times by new ERP questions just to say "done". | Agents other than ERP and mail no longer see the ERP's and mailbox's questions. They only get one if the ERP or mail agent gives up on it and it is handed to everyone. |
| C | The ERP agent re-opened pages it had just filed ("status didn't parse") because their facts were still being read. | After a `file_each`, the agent waits up to 10 s for those pages to be read before its next turn. |

**What "verification: steps visibly changed the page state" means:** after every browser action, our code reads the page again and compares it with the page before the action. It then tells the model either "visibly changed the page state" or "caused no visible page change". The comparison ignores the numbered ids, which change on every read.

- **Why it's there:** these portals often swallow a click or silently refuse a value. Without this line, the model would assume every action worked and keep going on a page that never changed. It's also how loops like "clicking a disabled link" get noticed.
- **What it costs:** one page re-read, about 0.3 s per action, and no model call. "Visibly changed" is the normal, good outcome. Only "caused no visible page change" points to a problem.
- **It isn't where the time goes.** In your log, nearly every slow part is a model turn: 2–3 s each, plus about 1 s waiting in the platform's queue. That's why these fixes target the number of turns.

When you run this version, check that the ERP's `file_each` lines include `"path": [...]` entries, and that the supplier-portal agent finishes soon after filing its requirements. Section 6 of `BEST_RUN_TIMING.md` has an empty row for the result.

how the cost is calculated here? is it depended on the model calls or how it is? Just tell me the direct answer in short.

Cost depends only on **tokens sent to and from the model**. The number of calls doesn't matter by itself, and browser time is free.

For Qwen, per million tokens:
- **Input: $0.15**
- **Cached input** (a prompt start the model has seen before): **$0.016**
- **Output: $0.47**

Your $0.223 run:
- 1.32M new input tokens × $0.15/M = **$0.198** (about 89% of the cost)
- 0.68M cached tokens × $0.016/M = $0.011
- 30k output tokens × $0.47/M = $0.014

So **input tokens are almost the whole bill**. Every call re-sends about 9k tokens (instructions, case file, history and the current page). Fewer calls and shorter prompts are therefore what cut the cost. The ranking then multiplies cost × time.

# Run ab00e578: three of four ERP file_each actions filed no stock or price page, so the model clicked them all again
# by hand (~8 turns per material, ERP 53 turns, investigation 302 s). Two causes, both handled in code here:
# 1. a label shown twice on a record page (once in the menu, once for the record): pick_control takes the one whose
#    address belongs to the record, or either one when both lead to the same address;
# 2. a notice page or dialog put in front of the record ("maintenance note ... accept and continue"): pass_notice
#    presses its single way forward, as the model does in its own turns, but only on a page without input fields.
NOTICE_PAGE = re.compile(r"hinweis|wartung|maintenance|notice|meldung|achtung|attention|information|bestätig|confirm",
                         re.I)
NOTICE_GO = re.compile(r"akzeptier|fortfahren|weiter|continue|accept|proceed|verstanden|got it|schließen|close|"
                       r"\bok\b|bestätigen|confirm", re.I)


def pick_control(page: str, label: str, kinds: tuple[str, ...], url: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """find_control, and when the label is ambiguous: the controls if they all lead to the same address, else the
    one control whose address carries a value of the current page's address (the record's own link)."""
    aid, why = find_control(page, label, kinds)
    if aid is not None or "controls are labelled" not in why:
        return aid, why
    ids = re.findall(r"\[(\d+)\]", why.split(":", 1)[0] if "):" in why else why)
    targets = {m.group(1): (re.search(r"->\s*(\S+)", m.group(4)) or [None, None])[1]
               for m in CONTROL.finditer(page) if m.group(1) in ids}
    addresses = set(targets.values())
    if len(addresses) == 1 and None not in addresses:
        return ids[0], why
    query = urlparse(url)
    tokens = [value for values in parse_qs(query.query).values() for value in values if len(value) >= 3]
    tokens += [part for part in query.path.split("/") if len(part) >= 4]
    scoped = [aid for aid, target in targets.items() if target and any(token in target for token in tokens)]
    if len(scoped) == 1:
        return scoped[0], why
    return None, why


async def pass_notice(tab, page: str) -> str | None:
    """A notice in front of the page (a dialog, or a short page that announces something) with a single way forward
    and no input field: press it and say what was pressed; None leaves the page as it is."""
    modal = "!! A MODAL DIALOG" in page
    area = page.split("!! END OF MODAL DIALOG")[0] if modal else page
    if not modal and (len(page) > 2500 or not NOTICE_PAGE.search(page)):
        return None
    controls = [(m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in CONTROL.finditer(area)]
    if any(kind.split("(")[0] in ("input", "select", "checkbox", "radio", "switch") for _, kind, _ in controls):
        return None  # a check to pass or a form to fill is the model's
    forward = list(dict.fromkeys(aid for aid, kind, label in controls
                                 if kind in ("button", "link", "clickable") and NOTICE_GO.search(label)))
    if len(forward) != 1:
        return None
    label = next(label for aid, _, label in controls if aid == forward[0])
    await tab.click(forward[0])
    return label

# Run ab00e578: three of four ERP file_each actions filed no stock or price page, so the model clicked them all again
# by hand (~8 turns per material, ERP 53 turns, investigation 302 s). Two causes, both handled in code here:
# 1. a label shown twice on a record page (once in the menu, once for the record): pick_control takes the one whose
#    address belongs to the record, or either one when both lead to the same address;
# 2. a notice page or dialog put in front of the record ("maintenance note ... accept and continue"): pass_notice
#    presses its single way forward, as the model does in its own turns, but only on a page without input fields.
NOTICE_PAGE = re.compile(r"hinweis|wartung|maintenance|notice|meldung|achtung|attention|information|bestätig|confirm",
                         re.I)
NOTICE_GO = re.compile(r"akzeptier|fortfahren|weiter|continue|accept|proceed|verstanden|got it|schließen|close|"
                       r"\bok\b|bestätigen|confirm", re.I)


def pick_control(page: str, label: str, kinds: tuple[str, ...], url: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """find_control, and when the label is ambiguous: the controls if they all lead to the same address, else the
    one control whose address carries a value of the current page's address (the record's own link)."""
    aid, why = find_control(page, label, kinds)
    if aid is not None or "controls are labelled" not in why:
        return aid, why
    listed = re.search(r"\(((?:\[\d+\](?:, )?)+)\): use their ids$", why)
    ids = re.findall(r"\[(\d+)\]", listed.group(1)) if listed else []
    targets = {m.group(1): (re.search(r"->\s*(\S+)", m.group(4)) or [None, None])[1]
               for m in CONTROL.finditer(page) if m.group(1) in ids}
    addresses = set(targets.values())
    if len(addresses) == 1 and None not in addresses:
        return ids[0], why
    query = urlparse(url)
    tokens = [value for values in parse_qs(query.query).values() for value in values if len(value) >= 3]
    tokens += [part for part in query.path.split("/") if len(part) >= 4]
    scoped = [aid for aid, target in targets.items() if target and any(token in target for token in tokens)]
    if len(scoped) == 1:
        return scoped[0], why
    return None, why


async def pass_notice(tab, page: str) -> str | None:
    """A notice in front of the page (a dialog, or a short page that announces something) with a single way forward
    and no input field: press it and say what was pressed; None leaves the page as it is."""
    modal = "!! A MODAL DIALOG" in page
    area = page.split("!! END OF MODAL DIALOG")[0] if modal else page
    if not modal and (len(page) > 2500 or not NOTICE_PAGE.search(page)):
        return None
    controls = [(m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in CONTROL.finditer(area)]
    if any(kind.split("(")[0] in ("input", "select", "checkbox", "radio", "switch") for _, kind, _ in controls):
        return None  # a check to pass or a form to fill is the model's
    forward = list(dict.fromkeys(aid for aid, kind, label in controls
                                 if kind in ("button", "link", "clickable") and NOTICE_GO.search(label)))
    if len(forward) != 1:
        return None
    label = next(label for aid, _, label in controls if aid == forward[0])
    await tab.click(forward[0])
    return label


async def file_each(tab, action: dict, file, saw, deadline: float, seen: str = "") -> str:
    """The file_each action: the model names several records on the page in front of it (links by id) and, if each
    record has tabs that matter, the tabs by label; code opens every record and tab and files it with the kind the
    model gave, then goes back to the list. The model chooses the records and kinds, as with keep; this only saves

Fixed and pushed (573bc3d), in the same folder. As before, I only checked that the files parse; nothing was run, and the fair-play scan is clean.

```bash
atira test-run D:/Personal_Projects/QuoteCraft-tier1/starter-kit --challenge rfq
```

**Why it cost less but took longer (`run_ab00e578`)**

- **Cost went down as planned.** The investigation cost $0.136 instead of $0.200. The tender agent dropped from 18 turns to 10 and the supplier portal from 40 to 12. The bid form entered 4 positions in a single turn.
- **Time went up because of the ERP.** It took 53 turns and finished at 5:01, so the investigation lasted 302 s instead of 178 s. In 3 of its 4 batch actions, the stock and price pages were **never filed**. The model then opened all of them again by hand, about 8 turns per material.
- **The model was also slower this run:** 2.9 s per call instead of 1.7 s, because of load on the shared queue.

**Why the batches failed and the ERP "halted" on the maintenance notice**

1. **Repeated label:** "VK13 · Konditionen anzeigen" appears twice on the material page, once in the menu and once for the material itself. The batch code refused to guess which one to click, so the stock and price paths stopped.
2. **The notice you saw** ("Wartungshinweis … Akzeptieren und fortfahren") popped up while **code** was opening a material in the batch. The model clicks "continue" without thinking in its own turns, but the batch code didn't know how. That record's paths failed, and you saw the ERP browser sitting on the notice.

**Fixes in round 6**

| Fix | What it does |
|---|---|
| Repeated labels | Takes the link that belongs to the open material (its address contains the material's ID), or either one if both go to the same place. Real ambiguity is still refused. |
| Notices | During a batch, a page whose **title or heading** says it's a notice, has **no input fields**, and offers exactly **one** "continue/accept" button gets that button clicked by code, then the step is retried. Access checks with sliders or fields stay with the model. |
| Shorter wait | After a batch, the agent waits 3 s instead of 10 s for its pages to be read. With a slow model, 10 s was costing up to 40 s. |

**Expected:** the ERP needs about 20 turns instead of 53, the investigation about 2–2.5 minutes, and the **total about 3:30–4:15**, at the same or lower cost.

def investigator(case: CaseFile, team: Team, tab: Tab, deadline: float) -> Agent:
    name = tab.site_id
    system = INVESTIGATOR.format(site=name, url=tab.base_url, brief=case.brief, actions=ACTIONS_HELP)

    def briefing() -> str:
        questions = questions_for_site(name, case.questions())
        news = case.take_news(name)
        text = f"CASE FILE\n{case.status()}\n\nOPEN QUESTIONS\n"
        text += "\n".join(f"- [{qid}] {question}" for qid, question in questions) or "(none)"
        if site_role(name) == "mail" and len(questions) >= 3:
            text += "\n\n" + MAIL_BATCH.format(count=len(questions))
        records = [qid for qid, _ in questions if qid.startswith(("material:", "data:"))]
        if site_role(name) == "erp" and len(records) >= 2:
            text += "\n\n" + RECORD_BATCH.format(count=len(records))
        if news:
            text += "\n\nNEWS FROM YOUR FILED DOCUMENTS\n" + "\n".join(f"- {item}" for item in news)
        own_pending = case.pending_for(name)
        if own_pending:
            text += f"\n\n({own_pending} filed document(s) are still being read.)"
        elif case.pending:
            text += f"\n\n({case.pending} document(s) filed by other agents are still being read.)"
        return text

    agent: Agent
    batched: dict = {}  # kind -> consecutive one-by-one filings, for the file_each nudge (#1)
    worked = [False]  # has filed something: from then on it may go idle by code once its questions are answered

    def finished_here() -> bool:
        """A routed (ERP or mail) agent that has worked and whose website has no open question left and nothing of

class Team:
    """Holds an agent that has nothing to do until the case file brings news, and ends the investigation when every
    agent is idle and no filed document is still being read."""

    def __init__(self, case: CaseFile, names: list[str], deadline: float):
        self.case, self.names, self.deadline = case, set(names), deadline
        self.idle: set[str] = set()
        self.finished = asyncio.Event()
        self.woken: dict[str, float] = {}  # when an agent was last woken for finished reading (at most every 30 s)

    def release(self, name: str, candidates: set[str]) -> None:
        """A routed agent (ERP or mail) went idle leaving `candidates` open and nothing is being read any more: those
        go to every agent (RELEASED), and the others are woken by a case-file change. Questions that turn up while it
        is idle are its own work (it is woken for them), so only the ones open when it went idle are candidates."""
        if self.case.pending or site_role(name) is None:
            return
        still = {qid for qid, _ in self.case.questions()} & candidates
        fresh = still - RELEASED
        if fresh:
            RELEASED.update(fresh)
            print(f"[{name}] left open, now offered to every agent: {', '.join(sorted(fresh))}", flush=True)
            bump = getattr(self.case, "_bump", None)
            if bump:
                bump()

    def hook(self, name: str):
        async def hold(why: str) -> str | None:
            before = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())}
            self.release(name, before)
            version = self.case.version
            # Documents still being read when the agent went idle: once one of them is done, the agent is woken if
            # questions are still open. Sandbox run 024bd2ac: the ERP agent went idle "until the requirements are
            # read" with its material questions already open; they were never new, so it slept for 400 s.
            reading = self.case.pending
            self.idle.add(name)
            try:
                while not self.finished.is_set() and time.time() < self.deadline:
                    changed = await self.case.wait_change(version, 1.0)
                    if self.finished.is_set():
                        break
                    if changed:
                        self.release(name, before)
                        version = self.case.version
                        fresh = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())} - before
                        # Fix #2: a routine "your document was read" notice does not wake an idle agent for another
                        # model turn (run 99f03f3f: the tender agent was woken 6 times only to say done again); new
                        # questions and notices that report a problem with its documents still do.
                        if fresh or any(NEEDS_ATTENTION.search(item) for item in self.case.news.get(name) or []):
                            return "The case file has news" + (f"; new open questions: {', '.join(sorted(fresh))}" if fresh else "") + "."
                        still_open = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())}
                        rested = time.time() - self.woken.get(name, 0.0) >= 30
                        if reading and self.case.pending < reading and still_open and rested:

                            return ("Documents that were still being read are now in the case file. Open questions: "
                                    f"{', '.join(sorted(still_open))}. Work on those your website can answer.")
                    elif self.idle == self.names and self.case.pending == 0:
                        self.finished.set()
                return None
            finally:
                self.idle.discard(name)

content.text: I'm checking the bid phase of run_2e081b8d to see what the browsers do after the tender form opens.

No. The bid page doesn't go back to the other websites for data. It types everything from memory. I checked the bid phase of run_2e081b8d (04:41 to 06:20):

**What happens when the tender form opens**
1. **04:41:** the investigation ends and the bid is calculated in memory: all 5 positions, prices, the 5% discount and the 356,949.62 total. This is the `BID: {...}` line in the log.
2. **04:41 to 06:01:** the clerk works only on the tender portal, typing straight from that bid: company, VAT number, email, the positions (4 of them filled in one action), discount and total.
3. **During the whole bid phase the customer portal and ERP browsers got zero inputs.** Nobody re-reads them.

**The one other website it does touch is the mailbox, and that's required:**
- **06:01:** the clerk clicks "TAN anfordern" (request TAN). The portal then emails a one-time code that didn't exist before that click, so it can't be in memory. Old codes in the mailbox are traps.
- **06:03 to 06:14:** the courier opens the mailbox, passes its robot check, reloads and reads the newest code. That's 3 model turns and about 13 s.
- When the bid phase starts, the code also opens a fresh tab in the mail browser in the background, with no model call, so the mailbox is already loaded when the code is needed. That's probably the "website opening again" you saw. It isn't fetching any data.

**Where the bid phase's 99 s actually go**

| Step | Time | Could it be cut? |
|---|---|---|
| Reaching the form (starts on the Q&A page, then goes to the overview, then to the bid form) | ~9 s, 2 turns | Slightly: start on the tender's main page |
| First position by hand: the "keine" certification option didn't exist, so the model retried with "Ohne Zertifizierung" | ~19 s, 2 turns | Some: one turn instead of two |
| 4 positions in one action | ~28 s, browser time only | Some: shorter waits between steps |
| Conditions, declarations, TAN request | ~11 s, 3 turns | Little |
| Courier gets the TAN | ~13 s, 3 turns | No: the robot check stays with the model under fair play |
| Enter the TAN, check, submit | ~6 s, 2 turns | No |

So at most about 15–20 s could come out of the bid phase. The big waste was the investigation (280 s), and mostly the mail agent's 50 turns, which round 7 targets.

        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:

        wanted = str(value)

                await self.settle()
                if await self._modal_is_open():
                    return "the page now has a modal dialog; read it before acting behind it"
                return f'selected "{wanted}" in [{aid}]'
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001

        options = await locator.evaluate("el => [...(el.options || [])].map(o => o.value + '=' + o.textContent.trim())")
        loose = [o.split("=", 1)[0] for o in options if wanted.lower() in o.lower()]
        if len(loose) == 1:

        locator = self._locator(aid)

        info = await self._describe(locator)

        try:

    async def settle(self):
        """Wait until the page, its frames and the data they fetch have arrived and nothing more is on its way."""
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        end, quiet = loop.time() + SETTLE_SECONDS, None

        while loop.time() < end:
